about: Corrections to 92N_NATIONAL_STATE_LOCAL_FISCAL_AUTHORITY.json found by Lane F's spec 9 spot check (data/research/money/government-budgets-2026.json, spotCheck92N; debt-and-credit-2026.json). 92N itself is research input and is not edited; a reader of 92N applies these on top of it. Approved by Claude CTO on 9/28/2026 at 4:57 a.m. EDT with the spec 9 research.

corrections.corrected: Indiana may carry an annual deficit into the next year and has no requirement to close it in the next cycle; the state still may not borrow except narrowly.
corrections.evidence: NASBO Budget Processes in the States (2021), balanced budget requirements table and state notes.

corrections.corrected: Spending above revenue that the rainy-day fund covers is carried into the next year, and that year's budget must cut to rebalance.
corrections.evidence: NASBO Budget Processes in the States (2021), balanced budget requirements table and state notes.

corrections.corrected: The governor may veto appropriation amounts line by line; the legislature overrides by a majority of elected members. 44 states have a line-item veto, not 43.
corrections.evidence: NASBO Budget Processes in the States (2021), Table 8; NCSL gubernatorial veto authority (44 states).

corrections.92N: Debt service capped at 9% of general state revenues (Art. VIII, section 1).
corrections.corrected: Debt service is capped at 8.25% of general state revenues through June 30, 2034, then 8%, under the 2012 amendment to Article VIII, section 1.
corrections.evidence: Wash. Const. Art. VIII, section 1, as amended by Engrossed Senate Joint Resolution 8221, approved by voters in November 2012 (resolution number from memory, to verify against the constitution text).
